A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FORGE research. Their text, equations, figures and tables support reliable comparison, including all nine appendix subsections in v5. v1 has no appendix.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 report original clustering, integrality-gap prediction, solver-guidance and PS-Gurobi augmentation experiments.

after.justification: v5 retains original empirical evaluations and adds appendix experiments on static features, strIPlib, codebook size, embedding arithmetic, solver configuration and SAT transfer.

M1.justification: The GraphSAGE/vector-quantization backbone and pretraining losses remain unchanged. The reported search-guidance procedure changes from top-5% positive candidates to top-decile candidates and describes separate negative-anchor neighborhoods; hard-negative selection changes from proximity to the positive variable to proximity to the anchor. Appendices A.5–A.6 add configuration-prediction heads and a SAT-specific input-feature variant using unchanged pretrained weights. These are limited adaptations of the existing framework.

E1.justification: v5 adds strIPlib evaluation across ten named optimization families, solver-configuration prediction using SCIP, and SAT/UNSAT-aware clustering on G4SATBench (A.2, A.5–A.6). This substantially expands task and domain coverage beyond the original optimization experiments. Figure 3 also changes the displayed difficulty groups, although its legend disagrees with the retained category list in Section 4.

E2.justification: v5 adds the Hutter et al. (2014) hand-crafted feature baseline to clustering and directly evaluates Cai et al. (2025a)'s multitask model for solver configuration (Figure 8; Table 3). These introduce substantive external comparisons absent from v1's experiments. The original mean-readout, label-propagation, Gurobi, Li et al. and PS-Gurobi comparisons remain; the random-feature PS-Gurobi control moves to Appendix A.8.

E3.justification: Section 4 changes the reported clustering test size from 1,050 to 1,000 instances. Added protocols include 500 strIPlib instances, codebooks ranging from 500 to 10,000 entries, embedding-arithmetic controls fixing graph size and solving difficulty, SCIP configuration evaluation, and 1,400 Hard SAT formulas grouped by problem type and feasibility. These substantially extend evaluation design; the original Gurobi time limits and principal training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 adds codebook-size sensitivity analysis, A.4 tests whether embedding arithmetic reflects covering/packing relationships, and A.6 compares unchanged MIP features with SAT-adapted features to isolate feature specialization. These address new questions about representation behavior and transfer. The pretraining-versus-scratch comparison and PS-Gurobi random-feature control already existed in v1; relocating the latter is not a new ablation.

E5.justification: Both versions average clustering NMI over ten k-means runs, and v1 Figure 3 already displays ± uncertainty terms. v5 extends that reporting convention to additional results without documenting a new uncertainty-estimation procedure, increased run count or seed policy. Appendix A.3's significance statement supplies no identifiable new test procedure.

E6.justification: Figure 3 changes mean-readout NMI from 0.087 to 0.726 and FORGE NMI from 0.843 to 0.953; changed sample counts and plotted categories prevent treating these as same-setting gains. New results include static-feature NMI 0.991, codebook sensitivity, SAT-transfer NMIs 0.76 and 0.77, and configuration runtimes—for example, 801.21 seconds for Cai et al. versus 670.95 for FORGE on CA. Original integrality-prediction errors and displayed solver-gain percentages are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix A.4 adds explicit covering/packing problem formulations, the vertex-cover/independent-set complement relation, and mathematical definitions of embedding centroids, difference vectors and translations in Equations 6–9. The original model losses and triplet-loss equation remain unchanged. No new theorem or proof establishing FORGE's capabilities is supplied; the GNN expressivity discussion summarizes prior work.

C1.justification: The central claim—solver-independent unsupervised MIP representations supporting multiple downstream tasks—remains. v5's conclusion extends claimed applicability to preliminary MIP-to-SAT transfer and qualifies FORGE as a step toward a foundational model. Replacing 'warm-start prediction' with 'search guidance' largely clarifies the existing variable-hint application rather than introducing a different central contribution.

C2.justification: Section 7 adds specific limitations concerning training scale, unexplored code semantics, solver integration and untested downstream applications. The appendices add interpretations of codebook insensitivity, covering/packing directions and cross-domain transfer. v5 also discusses the accuracy/computation tradeoff against strong hand-crafted features and distinguishes FORGE's sharing across problems from Cai et al.'s sharing across tasks, substantially refining the account of generalization.

D1.justification: Most hardware, learning rates, epochs and solver budgets were already disclosed and move to A.7. New details include Gurobi v12.0.3, equal BCE/triplet weighting, explicit PS-Gurobi retraining, and GPU-driven exclusion of very large training instances. A.1 and A.6 document baseline and SAT features. The stated release expands from code/pretrained weights to datasets, fine-tuned models and ready-made benchmark embeddings; availability is not independently verified.

R1.justification: Beyond relocating existing related work, v5 substantially expands positioning around GNN expressivity and foldable MILPs, hand-crafted instance features, algorithm selection and portfolios, online neighborhood search, and optimization-to-SAT transfer. New relevant works include Hutter et al.'s feature studies, Chen et al.'s MILP representation analysis, G4SATBench and Pal and Kadıoğlu's transfer work. Bibliographic duplicates and publication updates do not account for this substantive expansion.

P1.justification: v5 extensively rewrites the introduction and experimental narrative, consistently reframes warm starts as search guidance, merges numerical-results subsections into task descriptions, moves setup details to A.7, and splits related work between Section 6 and A.9. The former conclusion becomes a structured limitations/future-work discussion. These are substantial changes to the existing document's organization and exposition.

P2.justification: v5 adds static-feature, strIPlib, embedding-arithmetic and SAT plots plus three tables. Existing diagrams and solver plots are enlarged or relabeled, and Figure 3 is replotted with changed categories and axis labels. The original three-way PS-Gurobi plot is retained as Figure 14 while a two-method view appears in Figure 7. Typography, margins and figure placement are extensively revised.

improvement.justification: v5 substantially strengthens evaluation of the central general-purpose representation claim. The strong hand-crafted comparator, additional optimization and SAT domains, third downstream task and codebook ablation address important gaps in v1's validation; explicit limitations also better qualify the foundational-model framing. The revised clustering account remains insufficiently reconciled: Section 4 reports 1,000 instances and 21 groups, Figure 3 lists 20 groups, and A.3 uses 1,050 instances. Despite this reporting weakness and sparse statistical-test details, the broader, more discriminating evidence provides a substantial net quality improvement.
